A Zala Vármegyei Katasztrófavédelmi Igazgatóság közlése szerint a turistabusz és a pótkocsis teherautó a 86-os főúton, Keménfa közelében ütközött össze hajnali egy óra körül. A lengyel turistákat szállító buszon 53-an utaztak. A balesetben hatan könnyebben sérültek meg, köztük a teherautó vezetője is. A zalaegerszegi hivatásos és a zalalövői önkéntes tűzoltók biztosították a helyszínt, és gondoskodtak az utasok elhelyezéséről. Mivel a busz működésképtelenné vált, a sértetlen utasokat a zalalövői tornaterembe szállították, ahol a továbbutazásig várakozhattak. Augusztus 16-án lengyel zarándokokat szállító busz borult fel az M3-as autópályán Mezőkeresztesnél. Tizenkét ember meghalt , többen súlyosan megsérültek. https://www.cp24.com/news/entertainment/.text: In 2010, University of Toronto professor Anna Shternshis was researching the history of Yiddish culture in Ukraine during the Holocaust, when she came across a large collection of handwritten documents in the historic language spoken by Ashkenazi Jews. Many of them were poems, some with music notes next to them, dated between 1941 and 1947, which described life in Ukraine during, and after the Holocaust. “These were the times when their days were numbered,” Shternshis told CTVNews.ca in a video interview, about the poems written during the war. “So, everyone who created the song or a poem knew that they probably have a day or two to live. These materials either gave them comfort in those times or messages to the future.” Sixteen years later, those poems have been transformed into an album, titled “The Silenced Songs of World War II,” which recently won the German Record Critics’ Prize. But it took decades longer for them to be uncovered in the first place. Historic silencing The title references the silencing of the original documents, which were initially collected by scholar Moisei Beregovsky when he worked at the Ukrainian Academy of Science in the 1940s. He was arrested by former Soviet Union premier Joseph Stalin in the 1950s for the work that he did. At the time, Shternshis explained, Jews were not supposed to talk about being targeted in the Soviet Union during the Second World War. Shternshis said that since Beregovsky interviewed people who spoke of their suffering as a result of being Jewish, rather than Soviet citizens, he was arrested and sent to jail. “So, talking about (the) Holocaust seems like an anti-Soviet activity because so many people suffered, why single out Jews?” she said. Beregovsky’s research materials were confiscated and stored in KGB archives, until the collapse of the Soviet Union. Bringing ‘silenced’ music to life The project took more than a decade to come together since Shternshis had to do a lot of research to have the works translated, and then composed. She worked with 17 musicians, most of whom were Canadian, to bring the poems to life. In some cases, composers created music for the pieces, though most of the songs on the album have both original lyrics and tunes, which Shternshis described as “very simple folk songs.” However, the lyrics detailed a dark period, with many songs about pogroms, or riots, against Jews in Ukraine. “These materials are often the only Jewish eyewitness accounts of violence against them,” Shternshis said. “There are so many accounts of violence that come from perpetrators, and we very rarely hear victims themselves.” ”So these songs really document: ‘this is what happened. This is who came, these are the perpetrators. This is how they harassed us. This is how violence was committed. This is where it happened,’” she added. Common themes moving international audiences Shternshis has been able to stage concerts around the world, where the music’s lyrics are translated through subtitles of the local language. She said that the themes in the music bring up questions that relate to the regions, themselves. At a recent concert in Poland, many in the audience were Ukrainian refugees. Shternshis recalled one Ukrainian woman coming up to her after the concert to tell her she couldn’t believe how much the lyrics spoke to her. In South Korea, many audience goers had questions about themes of separation, the impossibility of return and how you keep the memory of life from disappearing. In China, there were questions about the idea of someone going to jail for a folk song. “The material that started as 100 per cent historical, became a lot more contemporary in some of its aspects,” she said. “There’s something about this material that is very local, it’s very focused on the time and a place where it happened, but also relates to people living through all sorts of different historical moments, including today.” However, the one place where Shternshis dreams of taking the music is back to where it was originally created. “Because of all the places in the world where we perform this, we have not done it in Ukraine,” she said. “It’s their history, the local history. Even though the Jewish community in Ukraine is very small, it doesn’t matter because it’s history of that place.”

Railbookers’ Famous Rivers by Rail collection features five independent holidays following the Rhine and Danube through some of Europe’s most popular destinations. Schneider Electric and Elsaco Electronic develop integrated electrical solutions for three major cogeneration projects in Romania (P) News Latest News Published on September 30, 2026 By Petre Barac Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Email Schneider Electric is expanding its more than 15-year collaboration with Elsaco Electronic by contributing to the development of electrical infrastructure for three major cogeneration projects in Romania: CET Hidrocarburi Arad (31.5 MWe), CET Palas Constanta (52 MWe) and CET Govora (52 MWe). The total value of the three projects exceeds 300 million euros. The projects aim to modernize and improve the efficiency of thermal and electrical energy generation infrastructure through the implementation of cogeneration systems. In this context, Schneider Electric is providing an integrated electrical solution covering a significant part of the infrastructure required for electrical power distribution, protection, monitoring and automation. Together with its partner Elsaco Electronic, Schneider Electric is supplying technologies across the main levels of the electrical infrastructure. The Schneider Electric solution includes PIX High medium-voltage switchgear, configured for power generation applications and equipped with dedicated generator circuit breakers, Okken low-voltage switchboards, Canalis busbar trunking systems, high-power Okken distribution switchboards, PrismaSeT distribution boards, as well as automation and motor control panels with variable speed drives for pump applications. For applications operating in high-temperature environments, the variable speed drives are installed in a flush-mount configuration, an approach that enables the solution to be adapted to demanding operating conditions while supporting the energy efficiency of motor-driven systems. The Schneider Electric solution also includes technologies for the automation and monitoring of the electrical infrastructure. Energy consumption management and monitoring are enabled by the Power Monitoring Expert (PME) platform, which collects and analyses data related to energy consumption and distribution, providing operators with greater visibility into the performance of the installation. At CET Arad, the Schneider Electric solution integrates the EcoStruxure Power Operation (EPO) electrical SCADA system, with advanced reporting capabilities provided by Power Monitoring Expert (PME), as well as PowerLogic T500 units for integration with higher-level SCADA systems. This enables the electrical infrastructure to be monitored and operated in an integrated manner, from medium- and low-voltage distribution through to communication with external energy management systems. The complexity of the power generation projects has also required specialized services for the configuration and verification of protection systems. Schneider Electric is providing protection coordination and calculation studies, as well as selectivity studies for high-, medium- and low-voltage installations. These services support the proper coordination of protection devices and contribute to improving the safety and availability of the electrical infrastructure. The studies are being carried out with the involvement of Schneider Electric specialists from France, together with the teams working on the projects in Romania. “The projects in Arad, Constanta and Govora demonstrate the value of a partnership in which expertise and technology come together to address complex requirements in the energy sector. For Schneider Electric, the objective was not only to provide individual pieces of equipment, but an integrated electrical solution covering everything from medium- and low-voltage distribution to automation, SCADA and energy management. At the same time, it is important that these projects have contributed to the development of relevant local capabilities for the digital transformation of energy infrastructure,” said Marius Tudor, Head of Sales Industrial EUs & Channels, Schneider Electric Romania. Strengthening local technical expertise An important outcome of the collaboration has been the development of Elsaco Electronic’s capabilities in advanced electrical solutions. As part of the projects, Elsaco teams have completed training programmes focused on implementing electrical SCADA solutions, while the company has also become a licensed partner for Okken solutions. “Our collaboration with Schneider Electric has enabled us to significantly strengthen the level of technical expertise we can provide in complex energy projects. Beyond the equipment delivered, the fact that our teams have developed expertise in electrical SCADA and that we have obtained licensing for Okken solutions represents an important benefit for both current and future projects. It is an investment in our ability to respond to the requirements of an energy market undergoing an accelerated transformation,” said Corneliu Bulibenchi, Technical Director, Elsaco Electronic. The partnership between Schneider Electric and Elsaco Electronic continues to support the development of solutions tailored to Romania’s energy infrastructure, combining international technology with locally developed expertise and capabilities.
